name: TEST-C
status: PRE-REGISTERED. Written and committed (with prereg.sha256) before any corpus-v4 candidate is screened, drawn or run, and before the harness-v1.8.0 tag is cut. Draw with: backend/.venv/Scripts/python.exe scripts/draw_corpus.py draw-v4 (after the harness-v1.8.0 tag, at that tag); run with reports/test-c/run_test_c.py at the frozen tag harness-v1.8.0.
purpose: A third, fresh pre-registered held-out test of RERUN, for harness-v1.8 (owner, directive 2026-10-07: 'a fresh pre-registered held-out test (TEST-C) ... 8-10 new repos, a committed selection rule that must NOT filter on fixability, thresholds from DEV evidence committed before the run, seal harness-v1.8.0, run once, audit, publish whatever comes out; report stratified by blocker family'). TEST, TEST-B and the out-of-sample scan stay frozen as published and are never re-run or re-scored under their old names; the 21 entries re-run as DEV-CONTAMINATED under harness-v1.8 (runs/dev_v18) are development evidence, not held-out, and are never pooled with TEST-C.
seed_note: The registration date, the convention of corpus-v1 (20260924), corpus-v2 (20260928) and corpus-v3 (20261005). Fixed before any corpus-v4 draw.
target_note: 10, the upper end of the owner's 8-10, so that the report stratified by blocker family has more than a handful of entries per family; the cost of 10 entries fits the ledger (run.test_c_cap_usd).

frame_and_population.rule: identical to corpus-v1, corpus-v2 and corpus-v3: the Papers-with-Code archive frame at the pinned revisions, the population file below, unchanged

eligibility.rule: E1-E4 identical to corpus-v1; E5_v2 identical to corpus-v2 and corpus-v3 (backend/app/batch/corpus_v2/prereg.json /eligibility: the same command_regex, placeholder_regex and command_rules exclusion rules). draw-v4 refuses to draw unless its regexes and command_rules equal corpus_v2/prereg.json's, as draw-v2 and draw-v3 do.
eligibility.no_fixability_filter: NOTHING in E1-E5_v2 looks at what a documented command NEEDS: no rule excludes a repository because it needs docker, conda, a licensed or private dataset, a GPU, a display, credentials, an unusual system package or a long run. The only exclusions are for a command that is not a RUN of the paper's code (an install, a download, a preprocessing or setup step, an unfilled placeholder: command_rules R1-R5) or a repository that is not Python or not reachable. Whether the command can be made to run is MEASURED by the run, and a repository RERUN cannot help is reported, in the stratum of its blocker family (analysis.stratified_by_blocker_family), not excluded. (Owner, 2026-10-07: 'The selection rule must not filter on fixability (no excluding docker, conda or licensed-data repos); report results stratified by blocker family instead.')
eligibility.known_limitation: Only the root README is searched (as corpus-v1); a README whose only run commands are excluded makes the paper ineligible, which shifts the sample toward repositories that document a direct run command; reported, not corrected.

firewall.rule: A candidate is skipped (logged as 'firewall') when its paper_url or its repository is already known to RERUN: (a) any paper_url or repo_url in corpus-v1, corpus-v2 or corpus-v3 corpus.yaml or screening_log.jsonl (every candidate ever screened, eligible or not); (b) any github.com/<owner>/<repo> found in any .json/.jsonl/.yaml/.yml/.md/.csv/.log/.txt file under runs/ or reports/ at the commit the draw runs on (every DEV, gate, TEST, TEST-B, seal, live UI, live-scan and harness-v1.8 DEV record and every report). Repositories are compared case-insensitively without a trailing '.git' or '/'. population.csv itself is not a firewall source (it lists the whole frame).
firewall.check_after_the_draw: draw-v4 recomputes the firewall after drawing and refuses to write corpus.yaml if any drawn entry is in it (a self-check, logged).

draw_procedure: random.Random(20261007).shuffle(list(range(len(population)))) in CPython; screen in that order with E3, E4, E5_v2; a firewalled candidate, or a repository already drawn for another paper, is skipped and logged; stop at 10 eligible or when the population is exhausted. Every draw is logged with its reason in screening_log.jsonl.
draw_script: scripts/draw_corpus.py draw-v4 (sealed in the harness-v1.8.0 tag with this file). It refuses to draw unless sha256(prereg.json) equals corpus_v4/prereg.sha256 and population.csv matches population_sha256.
corpus_hash_definition: sha256 of canonical JSON {prereg_sha256, entries sorted by name with name, repo_url, commit_sha, command} (as corpus-v1, corpus-v2 and corpus-v3)
harness: The TEST-C batch runs once on the tag harness-v1.8.0 with no harness change after the draw. No sandbox-touching file differs from the sealed harness-v1.7.1 / v1.7.2 (the seal rule of those releases: a release that changes no sandbox-touching file needs no paid seal; the sealed-batch preflight checks a clean tree, a pushed tag and that the harness paths equal the tag). A harness defect found by TEST-C is recorded as a known limit, not fixed; nothing is re-run and nothing is tuned on a TEST-C result.

run.arm: treatment (full RERUN: repair, Tavily, the deterministic rules), each entry ONCE, in ascending id
run.cap_note: 10 entries x $2.50 = $25.00 worst case for the entries; the rest ($75.00 or more) funds the D-42 sustained runs (600 s each at most, about $9.12 at $0.0152/s), shared equally among the entries that need one: the same structure as TEST-B ($95.00 for 8 entries). Ledger ceiling $300.00 API-reported (the ledger stood at $129.91 on 2026-10-07, so the worst case after is $229.91), BILLED floor $10.00 (balance $44.37 on 2026-10-07). The worst case is printed before the run (reports/ledger_total.py).
run.cap_stops: An entry the entry cap stops (INDETERMINATE COST_CAP) is reported as such, in its own stratum; the cap is not raised for it, so that TEST-C stays comparable with TEST-B (owner's cap, unchanged).
run.infra_retry: an entry that ends INFRA_ERROR with no baseline execution is re-run ONCE (the first record kept unmodified under infra_retries/), as in the TEST phase and TEST-B; no other re-run exists

analysis.primary_measure: RAN: the number of the 10 entries whose documented command actually ran, under the rule below. A count over 10 entries, one run each: not a rate. It does not say that any paper's result was reproduced.
analysis.ran_rule: identical to corpus-v3 /analysis/ran_rule (R1-R4) and its D-46 audit (corpus_v3/prereg.json /analysis/d46_audit), unchanged: R1 a RUNS_* verdict; R2 confirmed (the documented command exited 0 by itself, or its sustained run completed with exit 0, or ran the full 600 s without failing and without a funding limit); R3 for the first two forms the final run printed something; R4 not struck by the D-46 audit (a pipe whose first command did not run to completion; a traceback, a Python exception line, a usage message or a missing-credential message in the final output). The audit can only strike an entry, never add one; each strike is stated with the line that caused it. Reported beside RAN, never added to it: SEMANTIC CHANGE, RESOURCE-ADAPTED and SOLE CANDIDATE entries, and a second line without semantic change.

diagnosis_measure.name: actionable diagnosis
diagnosis_measure.what: m of M: of the M entries whose verdict is not RUNS_CLEAN / RUNS_AFTER_REPAIR (BLOCKED, INDETERMINATE, TIMEOUT; an entry struck by the audit is one of them), the number whose stored diagnosis meets all four criteria of the written rubric reports/dev/v18/DIAGNOSIS_RUBRIC.md (A1 verbatim line, A2 the cause the key proves, A3 a concrete next action, A4 anchored in the final state).
diagnosis_measure.scored_by: reports/dev/v18/score_diagnosis.py against an answer key written from each record's RAW LOG before any blocker text is read, committed, and only then scored (the rubric's Procedure). The rubric, the scorer and the procedure are committed with this file and are not changed after the draw.
diagnosis_measure.reported: beside RAN, never merged with it, as two figures each with its own definition; per blocker family; with the per-set medians of wall-clock time and API-reported cost to a diagnosis and the recovery rate (reports/dev/v18/set_metrics.py, committed records only).

analysis.stratified_by_blocker_family: Every non-running entry is reported under the family of its blocker report (Dependencies, Environment, Resources, Inputs, Data, Documentation, Code), with the count of entries and, for each, how many were actionable; an entry the cap stopped is shown in its own line (COST_CAP). Nothing is pooled across families into a rate that hides a family.

thresholds_from_dev_evidence.source: reports/dev/v18/dev_results.json, diagnosis_dev_score.json and set_metrics.json, committed 2026-10-07 before this registration. The 21 DEV entries are repositories the harness-v1.8 fixes were written from, so every DEV figure is an upper bound for what a fresh set should show.

dev_evidence.ran: DEV corpus re-run: 2 of 16 audited RAN (v1.5 TEST 1 of 8, v1.7.2 TEST-B 1 of 8): no entry moved from not-running to running
dev_evidence.actionable_diagnosis_as_the_dev_runs_sto: 9 of 18 (50 percent): new runs of repositories the rules were written from
dev_evidence.actionable_diagnosis_as_the_current_rule: 16 of 18, a fit (the rules were corrected from those records)

claims: DIAGNOSIS: the claim 'harness-v1.8's diagnosis is actionable' is made only if m is at least 50 percent of M (the DEV as-stored figure: 5 of 10 if all ten are non-running). Below that, TEST-C reports that the claim is NOT supported and says which family and which criterion failed.

RUN RATE: no target for RAN, as in TEST-B. A claim that harness-v1.8 RAN more than harness-v1.7.2 is made only if RAN is at least 3 of 10 (30 percent), above the 1 of 8 (12.5 percent) of both earlier fresh sets and the 2 of 16 (12.5 percent) of the DEV re-run. Otherwise TEST-C reports that no improvement in RAN is shown.
COST: no claim about cost; the per-set medians are reported.
Small N: ten entries, one run each. These are counts with a stated threshold, not estimates of a rate, and a result near a threshold is reported as near it.

analysis.target: none for RAN; the diagnosis and run-rate claims above are the only thresholds
analysis.beside_it: TEST (harness-v1.7.1 code), TEST-B (harness-v1.7.2) and the out-of-sample scan are frozen and never pooled with TEST-C; the DEV-CONTAMINATED re-runs are never pooled with it.
